title: 好久不见  (Long Time No See)

segments.t: That evening in a quiet lounge, Chun Yuqiao runs into his former colleague and current rival Xie Ling, whose competing music show tapes in three days. Listen to their icy banter first.
好久不见，你也在这儿？
你不也在这儿呢吗？
介绍一下，老同事，淳于乔。
再过三天就要开始录了，准备好了吗？
我有点替你担心啊。
如果是你的话，就不会担心别人的事了。
谢总有进步啊。
我看是你退步了。
如果你真的要尹正宇的话，我让给你啊。
真的？
Now let's unpack every line of this rival showdown.
好久不见，你也在这儿？
'Long time no see — you are here too?' Classic greeting "haojiu bu jian" literally says 'good long time not see' — in fact, English 'long time no see' was borrowed straight from Chinese!
你不也在这儿呢吗？
'Are you not right here too?' Slipping "bu" before "ye", 'also', in "ni bu ye zai zher ne ma?" parries Xie Ling's question with cool 'aren't you here too?'.
介绍一下，老同事，淳于乔。
'Let me introduce him: my old colleague, Chun Yuqiao.' Use "jieshao" in "jieshao yixia" whenever you introduce someone, and "tongshi" for a colleague or coworker.
再过三天就要开始录了，准备好了吗？
'In three more days taping starts — are you ready?' Express 'in three more days' with "zai guo santian", literally 'pass three days again', followed by "zhunbei hao le ma?", 'are you ready?'.
我有点替你担心啊。
'I am a little worried on your behalf.' Preposition "ti" before a person means 'for' or 'on behalf of' — here mock concern in "ti ni danxin", 'worry for you'.
如果是你的话，就不会担心别人的事了。
'If I were in your shoes, I would not worry about other people's business.' Notice the frame "ruguo... de hua" for 'if...', while "bieren" means 'other people'.
谢总有进步啊。
'Director Xie has made progress.' That is faint, cutting praise: "jinbu", literally 'step forward', means progress or improvement.
我看是你退步了。
'Looks to me like you are the one who has slipped backward.' Swap "jin", 'advance', for its opposite "tui", 'retreat', and "jinbu" flips cleanly into "tuibu", 'fall behind' or 'regress'.
如果你真的要尹正宇的话，我让给你啊。

'If you really want Yin Zhengyu, I will let you have him.' Earlier "rang" meant 'ask' or 'let someone do'; followed by "gei", the expression "rang gei ni" means yield or concede a prize to someone else.
真的？
'Really?' Here is a two-syllable word for 'really?' that every learner uses on day one: rising "zhende" asks 'for real?' or 'truly?'. Now let's listen to the whole lounge confrontation again.
好久不见，你也在这儿？
你不也在这儿呢吗？
介绍一下，老同事，淳于乔。
再过三天就要开始录了，准备好了吗？
我有点替你担心啊。
如果是你的话，就不会担心别人的事了。
谢总有进步啊。
我看是你退步了。
如果你真的要尹正宇的话，我让给你啊。
真的？

Why would Chun Yuqiao hand Yin Zhengyu to his fiercest rival? Xie Ling takes the bait, setting off alarm bells back at Xingtian. You learned "haojiu bu jian", opposite pair "jinbu" and "tuibu", and "zhen de?".
再见！
